title: Interpreting a confidence interval

draft.title: Interpreting a confidence interval
card: The true proportion p is a fixed number. Different random samples give different p-hat values, so they give different intervals.
The 95% describes the method. If we took many random samples and made an interval from each, about 95% of the intervals would contain p.
Any one interval either contains p or it does not. We do not know which, but the method works about 95% of the time.
A larger sample size n gives a narrower interval, so p is pinned down more closely. The 95% level stays the same.
draft.remember: 95% describes how often the method captures p. Larger samples give narrower intervals.

a.q: A poll of Geelong residents gives a 95% confidence interval of 0.42 to 0.52 for the proportion who support a new bike path. What does the 95% mean?
opts: About 95% of such intervals contain the true proportion
95% of Geelong residents support the bike path
95% of sample proportions fall between 0.42 and 0.52
The sample proportion is 95% likely to equal the true one
a.why: The 95% describes the long run of intervals made by the same method, and about 95% of them contain the true proportion. It is not a percentage of residents, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Think about many polls, not just this one.

b.q: Hana surveys 100 students and Leo surveys 400 students from the same school, and their p-hat values are close. Both make 95% intervals. Which interval is likely narrower?
opts: Leo's, because a larger sample varies less
Hana's, because a smaller sample is more precise
Leo's, because his interval is more likely to contain p
Neither, because both are 95% intervals so widths match
b.why: A larger sample varies less from sample to sample, so Leo's interval is narrower. Both methods capture p about 95% of the time, so the confidence level does not make Leo's interval more likely to contain p.
b.clue: Both use 95%. What differs is the sample size.

a.best: About 95% of such intervals contain the true proportion

b.best: Leo's, because a larger sample varies less
